entries.name: Giant kelp
entries.leaves: blades up to 80 cm with gas bladders at the base
entries.voxel_shape: tall central stipe from a holdfast, many ribbon blades with floating bladders, surface canopy
entries.notes: Forms vast underwater forests; the fastest-growing organism known in good conditions. Fronds live only months but holdfasts persist for years.

entries.name: Common eelgrass
entries.leaves: long flat ribbons 20-80 cm long in ordinary beds, up to 2 m in rich ones
entries.voxel_shape: undulating underwater meadow of long green ribbons rooted in sediment
entries.notes: True flowering plant, not an algae. Meadows buffer coasts and are keystone habitat; 'wasting disease' killed huge beds in the 1930s.

entries.name: Sargassum
entries.leaves: small serrated blades with air bladders, never anchored
entries.flowers: rarely seen; reproduces mostly by fragmentation
entries.fire: burns when piled dry on beaches
entries.voxel_shape: floating tangled mats of branching yellow-brown fronds with round air bladders
uses: floating nursery habitat for turtles and fish
entries.notes: Free-floating, never touches the seabed; gives the Sargasso Sea its name. Since 2011 huge rafts have flooded Caribbean and Atlantic shores.

entries.name: Sea lettuce
entries.leaves: thin translucent green sheets, two cell layers thick
entries.voxel_shape: crinkled bright green sheets hanging in the water or lying flat
entries.notes: Almost everywhere and almost impossible to kill; a sign of nutrient-rich water. Extremely fast growing.

entries.name: Oarweed
entries.leaves: long thick stipe splitting into wide palm-like fronds
entries.voxel_shape: stout tough stipe from a root-like holdfast, broad digitate fronds reaching the surface
entries.notes: The classic kelp of rocky Atlantic shores; a historical source of iodine for medicine.

entries.name: Sugar kelp
entries.leaves: one long undivided blade with a wavy edge, sweet tasting
entries.voxel_shape: single broad gold-brown blade on a short holdfast, low underwater forest
entries.notes: Tastes sweet when fresh; currently farmed at scale in the North Sea as a food and feed crop.

entries.name: Kombu
entries.leaves: long dark blade, cultivated and harvested young
entries.voxel_shape: very long dark blades on strings in farms; wild beds in cold shallow seas
entries.notes: The dashi seaweed; harvested from the cold seas of Hokkaido. Wild Rishiri form is prized for clear soup stock.

entries.name: Dulse
entries.leaves: leathery red-purple blades with flattened lacy lobes
entries.voxel_shape: short red hand-sized blades clinging to lower shore and subtidal rocks
entries.notes: The Irish/Scots 'dillisk'; traditionally picked by hand on the low shore and eaten dry as a snack.

entries.name: Nori
entries.leaves: thin purple-black sheets cultivated on nets
entries.voxel_shape: thin dark sheets drying to paper-like nori after net cultivation
entries.notes: The entire Japanese sushi industry depends on this one crop; farmed on nets in shallow bays.

entries.name: Laver
entries.leaves: thin dark sheets on the upper shore
entries.voxel_shape: dark purple papery sheets on wave-washed rocks at high tide line
entries.notes: Wales' 'laverbread' is simmered laver; hand-gathered on the upper shore for generations.

entries.name: Wakame
entries.leaves: olive blade with ruffled midrib and a finger-like reproductive sporophyll
entries.voxel_shape: wavy olive blade 30 cm to 3 m with a crinkled golden base spur
entries.notes: Soup seaweed; aggressively naturalised worldwide from ballast and aquaculture escapes - a flagship invasive seaweed.

entries.name: Bull kelp
entries.leaves: one bullwhip stipe topped by a single gas bladder and 4-5 m blade clusters
entries.voxel_shape: single whippy rope rising to one round float at the surface with ribbon blades
entries.notes: Annual; a kelp forest can appear and vanish within a couple of years. One float per plant is the giveaway against giant kelp.

entries.name: Neptune grass
entries.leaves: flat ribbons 5-12 mm wide in dense underwater meadows, bar-shaped leaves
entries.voxel_shape: dense Mediterranean seagrass meadow, waist-high ribbons, dead banquettes wash ashore
uses: historic roof insulation (balls of leaf fibre)
entries.notes: The oldest living organism on Earth: a Formentera meadow was aged at 80,000-200,000 years. Grows ~1 cm of rhizome a year and cannot recover once destroyed.

entries.name: Turtle grass
entries.leaves: flat ribbons 4-12 mm wide with rounded tips
entries.voxel_shape: tropical underwater meadow of flat green blades on white sand flats
entries.notes: Principal food of green turtles in the Caribbean; its presence marks healthy shallow sand.

entries.name: Manatee grass
entries.leaves: cylindrical hollow blades like green spaghetti
entries.voxel_shape: meadow of thin round green blades mixed with turtle grass beds
entries.notes: Hollow round leaves make ID easy; often the second species in Caribbean seagrass mixed beds.

entries.name: Spoon seagrass
entries.leaves: small oval leaves in pairs on slender stems
entries.voxel_shape: low dense mat of small oval leaves hugging the seabed
entries.notes: Favored dugong forage; small enough to carpet whole sandy bays almost flat.

entries.name: Surfgrass
entries.leaves: very narrow straps anchored by grappling-hook roots to rock and shell
entries.flowers: small, submerged, release ribbon-like pollen underwater
entries.voxel_shape: narrow green ribbons waving from intertidal rock in pounding surf
entries.notes: One of the few seagrasses that anchors to rock and lives in the wave-battered intertidal.

entries.name: Bladderwrack
entries.leaves: forking olive fronds with paired air bladders
entries.voxel_shape: mid-tide band of branching olive fronds with paired bladdery floats
uses: historically burned for soda ash and iodine
entries.notes: The wrack of every rocky shore; the source of the old kelp-burning soda industry. Thalli live a few years.

entries.name: Knotted wrack
entries.leaves: long beaded fronds with bladders in a single unbranched chain
entries.voxel_shape: fat knotted chains hanging from upper shore rocks at low tide
entries.notes: Grows only millimetres to a centimetre per year and can live for many decades; harvest quotas exist because beds recover slowly.

entries.name: Cuvie
entries.leaves: stiff upright fronds with a rigid rough stipe, dense 'kelp forests'
entries.voxel_shape: yard-tall stiffer forest of dark fronds below low water
entries.notes: Stiffer than oarweed; its dense offshore forests shelter huge numbers of lobster and fish.

entries.name: Dabberlocks
entries.leaves: long undivided blade with a corrugated midrib and a small winged reproductive frond
entries.voxel_shape: long rippling arrow-like blades streaming in current from wave-battered rock
entries.notes: A flagship of Icelandic seaweed cuisine; lives in the most wave-exposed zones.

entries.name: Sea palm
entries.leaves: single flexible stipe topped by a crown of long straps, palm-tree silhouette
entries.voxel_shape: miniature palm wave at low tide on exposed headland ledges
uses: ecological indicator of healthy surf zones
entries.notes: Briefly resembles a palm tree at low tide; annual and wholly restricted to pounding open coast.

entries.name: Feather boa kelp
entries.leaves: long stipe studded with alternating blades and bladders, like a feather boa
entries.voxel_shape: long whippy chains of small blades and floats streaming from rocks
entries.notes: Occurs from the low intertidal to the open kelp forest; blades and bladders alternate like a feather boa.

entries.name: Wireweed
entries.leaves: long perennial primary axis with short side branches and small air bladders
entries.voxel_shape: wiry ankle-to-metre brown alga, anchored on rocks or broken drifting
entries.notes: Introduced from Japan to Europe and America by the 1970s; now choking marinas and eelgrass beds in the North Sea and Channel.

entries.name: Gracilaria
entries.leaves: thin many-branched axes, red to greenish depending on light
entries.voxel_shape: bushy free-branching red axes in warm shallow bays, often farmed on ropes
entries.notes: One of the world's main agar crops; quality of the jelly sets it apart for microbiology and food.

entries.name: Kappaphycus
entries.leaves: stout knobby red branches farmed on long lines in warm shallow water
entries.voxel_shape: knobby red bushes strung on long-line farms in clear tropical shallows
entries.notes: Most of the world's carrageenan comes from this farmed red alga; a lifeline cash crop for coastal villages.

entries.name: Sea grapes
entries.leaves: upright stems of bright green grape-like beads
entries.voxel_shape: low mat of green bead-strings, like grapes growing underwater
entries.notes: One single gigantic cell; pops like caviar when eaten fresh with vinegar or soy.

entries.name: Killer algae
entries.leaves: creeping stolons with feathery green fronds exuding toxins
entries.voxel_shape: low spreading feathery green carpet smothering the seabed
entries.notes: Escaped from an aquarium in Monaco in 1984; blankets Mediterranean seabeds where native posidonia once grew.

entries.name: Irish moss
entries.leaves: small branching red fronds, cartilaginous, rainbow in strong light
entries.voxel_shape: hand-sized fan of red-purple branches on the low shore rocks
uses: carrageenan (used in Irish moss drinks, blancmange)
entries.notes: The original source of carrageenan for Irish moss blancmange and warming drinks.

entries.name: Asparagopsis
entries.leaves: tiny fern-like white-pink feathery fronds, strikingly soft
entries.voxel_shape: delicate pink-white feathery tufts on warm rocks among other algae
entries.notes: Feeding a tiny fraction to cattle cuts methane emissions dramatically; one of the most watched seaweeds in climate research.

entries.name: Maerl
entries.leaves: freely living branched pink coralline fronds, no attachment
entries.voxel_shape: gravelly pink gravel bed of free-rolling coralline branches on the seabed
entries.notes: Builds pink 'coral gravel' beds that take centuries to form and shelter extraordinary biodiversity; harvest is now restricted.

entries.name: Coral weed
entries.leaves: articulated pink-white calcified joints, coral-pink in sun
entries.voxel_shape: small crusting pink fans in rock pools, chalky to the touch
entries.notes: Calcified and brittle; responsible for the pink encrusting films on rocks and for building coralline reefs.

entries.name: Halimeda
entries.leaves: chains of round calcified segments, leaves like hard coins on a stem
entries.voxel_shape: lumpy lime-green grape bunches of hard calcified plates
uses: sand formation on coral reefs (produces much white sand)
entries.notes: When it dies its calcified segments crumble into the white sand of tropical beaches and reefs.

entries.name: Mermaid's wineglass
entries.leaves: single-cell stalk topped by a parasol-shaped cap
entries.voxel_shape: tiny parasol mushrooms of translucent green scattered over warm rock
uses: classic model organism in biology labs
entries.notes: One cell that grows up to 10 cm tall - proof a single cell can reach centimetre scale; history's favourite genetics demo.

entries.name: Dead man's fingers (algae)
entries.leaves: felty dark green cylindrical fingers, spongy
entries.voxel_shape: dark felty green fingers up to a metre, gripping low rocks and shell hash
entries.notes: Native to Japan; spread around the world and smothers shellfish beds - named, confusingly, after the soft coral of the same English name.

entries.name: Emiliania huxleyi
entries.leaves: one microscopic cell armoured in limestone discs (coccoliths)
entries.voxel_shape: none measurable; builds vast milky turquoise blooms visible from space
entries.notes: Billions per litre; its blooms turn the sea turquoise and their chalk ancestors built the white cliffs of Dover.

entries.name: Sea sawdust
entries.leaves: filaments of cyanobacteria bundled into rusty rafts smaller than a grain of rice
entries.voxel_shape: none measurable; rusty flecks on the surface of warm seas
uses: fixes nitrogen for the whole tropical ocean
entries.notes: Named 'erythraeum' for the Red Sea; feeds the tropics with nitrogen by fixing it from the air.

entries.name: Karenia brevis
entries.leaves: microscopic dinoflagellate with a whip-like flagellum
entries.voxel_shape: none measurable; causes red tides that kill fish and aerosolise toxins ashore
entries.notes: The Gulf of Mexico red tide; brevetoxin aerosol stings eyes and throats on beaches up to a mile from the shore.

entries.name: Driftwood fungus
entries.leaves: microscopic black fruiting bodies (ascomata) studding sand grains on driftwood
entries.voxel_shape: black specks on sand-encrusted driftwood and shells at the tide line
uses: decomposes beached wood and plant litter
entries.notes: The most frequently reported marine fungus on Earth; an arenicolous (sand-loving) ascomycete living on driftwood and seafoam.
